title: How to start a drive at your school · AquaTerra
description: How AquaTerra has run drives at schools: one skill, a small team, a day agreed with the school and a write-up after. {count} school drives since {firstYear}.
lede: A school drive works best when it is built around one skill and agreed with the school first. AquaTerra has written up {count} drives at schools since {firstYear}, from maths and science workshops to plantation days and festival crafts. The steps below come from how those drives actually ran.

sections.heading: plan one skill and one day
body: Pick one skill and one day before you talk to anyone else. Table Time, a maths tables workshop at School On Wheels HUHT in May 2023, was built around a single skill: multiplication tables. Think and Tinker, a science workshop at the same school in March 2025, did the same with simple experiments. One clear skill tells the school exactly what the children will take away.

Plantation days use the same logic. Grow Green ran plantation drives at Ashok Hall School in August 2023 and again in August 2025, and the 2025 drive planted a hundred saplings with eleven volunteers. Speak to Shine ran as two days at School On Wheels HUHT, on 11 May and 22 June 2023, so a team that likes its first session can plan a second.

sections.heading: agree it with the school
body: Talk to the school about the room, the day and what the children are already learning. The workshops on this page sat close to classroom subjects: maths tables, science basics, speaking and storytelling, and origami as a hands-on way into patience and focus. Ask a teacher what the class is working on this term, and build the session around it.

Keep the team small. Most of the workshops on this page had between two and five volunteers, which lets each volunteer sit with a few children. The Rakhi Loom workshop at South Calcutta Inner Wheel School in August 2023 had four volunteers, and its write-up says fifty children were taught.

sections.heading: run the session in a clear order
body: Open with something the children know, teach the skill, and finish with a game or a story. Tale Time at School On Wheels Belgachia in March 2025 built its stories from guided prompts, so every child had somewhere to start. Speak to Shine's write-up describes shy voices becoming storytellers over its two days.

Make the skill something the children do with their hands. Origami Time folded paper into birds and boats at School On Wheels Park Circus in March 2025. Waste Wise used games, demonstrations and storytelling to build eco habits at Ashok Hall School in August 2023. A session with something to make, or a game to play, gives the children a reason to stay in the room.

sections.heading: write it up and go back
body: Write the drive up the same week: the school, the date, the skill, the team and how many children came. AquaTerra's write-ups go on the site, so the next team can see what a school session looked like before it plans its own. A short write-up that names the skill is a useful thing to leave behind.

Go back when it works. South City International School hosted five drives on this page, from the Grow Green plantation drives in April 2025 to the Morpheus days in July 2025, which ran over two days at the same school. Repeat visits let a team learn the school's routine. Students who want a drive like this can join AquaTerra through the [join page](/join) and plan it with a team.

learnings: Agree one skill and one day with the school before you plan anything else.
Two to five volunteers was the usual size for a school workshop, enough for each one to sit with a few children.
Plantation days and workshops ran at the same schools, so a school that liked one could host the other.
Write each drive up the same week, while the details are still clear.

faqs.q: How do I start a drive at my school?
faqs.a: Start with one skill, one day and a small team of volunteers, then agree the room and the date with the school. The steps on this page come from the {count} school drives AquaTerra has written up since {firstYear}. Students who want to take part can start on the join page.

faqs.q: How many volunteers does a school drive need?
faqs.a: Most school workshops AquaTerra has written up had two to five volunteers, enough for each one to sit with a few children. Plantation days and Roots days had more, between five and twelve volunteers.

faqs.q: What kind of drive works at a school?
faqs.a: Workshops in maths, science, speaking, storytelling, origami and art have all run at schools, along with plantation drives and festival crafts. The best guide is what the school already teaches, so the session fits the class rather than competing with it.

faqs.q: Which schools has AquaTerra run drives at?
faqs.a: Schools on this page include South City International School, School On Wheels HUHT, Ashok Hall School, South Calcutta Inner Wheel School and Calcutta Boys School. In all, the drives on this page took place at {placesCount} places, and several of them were schools.

faqs.q: Can AquaTerra run a drive at my school?
faqs.a: Schools can host AquaTerra workshops and drives, and the write-ups on this page show what those looked like. To talk about a visit, get in touch through the contact page.
